e-7641.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance Given the Number, Sum, and Sum of Squares of the Data Points
e-7641.problem:
Compute the variance $\sigma^2$ of a data set $x_i$ consisting of $8$ data points, where

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320.
$$
e-7641.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the variance of the data set is given by 

$$
\sigma^2 = \overline{x^2} - (\overline{x})^2,
$$

where $\overline{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overline{x^2}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=8$ points in our data set, and we know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i = 40,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 40 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ We know that $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^{8} x_i^2 = 320,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}{\sum }_{i=1}^{8}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 320 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =40-{(5)}^{2} \\  & =40-25 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7639.problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
4, \: 5, \: 4, \: 7, \: 8, \: 11, \: 3
$$
e-7639.worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
\sigma^2 = \overline{x^2} - (\overline{x})^2,
$$

where $\overline{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overline{x^2}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (4+5+4+7+8+11+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 42 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot ({4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{7}^{2}+{8}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (16+25+16+49+64+121+9) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 300 \\  & =\frac{300}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{300}{7}-{(6)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{300}{7}-36 \\  & =\frac{300-252}{7} \\  & =\frac{48}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-7640.knowledge_point: Computing the Standard Deviation of a Data Set
e-7640.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7, \: 5, \: 0, \: 2, \: 1, \: 3
$$
e-7640.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})^2 } = \sqrt{ \,\,\, \vphantom{\sum\limits_{i=1}^n} \overline{x^2} - \left( \overline{x} \right)^2 }
$$

First, let's compute $\overline{x}.$ There are $n=6$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (7+5+0+2+1+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot 18 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overline{x^2}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot (49+25+0+4+1+9) \\  & =\frac{88}{6} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{44}{3}-9 \\  & =\frac{44-27}{3} \\  & =\frac{17}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{ \sigma^2 } = \sqrt{ \dfrac{17}{3} }.
$$

content.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7,\,3,\,3,\,5,\,1,\,0,\,2
$$
content.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=7$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (7+3+3+5+1+0+2) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot 21 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\cdot (49+9+9+25+1+0+4) \\  & =\frac{97}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{97}{7}-{(3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{97}{7}-9 \\  & =\frac{97-63}{7} \\  & =\frac{34}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{34}{7}}.
$$

after.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
1,\,1,\,5,\,4,\,9
$$
after.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (1+1+5+4+9) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 20 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{9}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (1+1+25+16+81) \\  & =\frac{124}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{124}{5}-{(4)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{124}{5}-16 \\  & =\frac{124-80}{5} \\  & =\frac{44}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{44}{5}}.
$$

after.name: Question 19
after.problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
7,\,4,\,11,\,2,\,6
$$
after.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (7+4+11+2+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 30 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({7}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{11}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (49+16+121+4+36) \\  & =\frac{226}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{226}{5}-{(6)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{226}{5}-36 \\  & =\frac{226-180}{5} \\  & =\frac{46}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{46}{5}}.
$$

after.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-7+3-5-1-5) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-15) \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [(-7)^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-5)^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [49+9+25+1+25] \\  & =\frac{109}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{109}{5}-{(-3)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{109}{5}-9 \\  & =\frac{109-45}{5} \\  & =\frac{64}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{64}{5}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{8\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
